stem: Aarav starts with a full bottle. He pours out $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of the bottle, then pours out $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of what remains.

parts.text: Which claim correctly tracks the amount poured the second time?

options.text: The second pour is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the original full bottle.
After the first pour, $\dfrac{4}{5}$ remains; the second pour is $\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5}$ of the original.
The remaining part produces the original whole, so the second pour is $\dfrac{1}{4} \div \dfrac{4}{5}$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The second fraction applies to the current remaining amount 4/5, not to the original full bottle.

teacher.key_rationale: After removing 1/5, 4/5 remains; the next "of" multiplies that current whole: (1/4)×(4/5)=1/5. Taking 1/4 of the original omits the updated whole. Dividing by 4/5 reverses the remaining-part relation.
